2607.17883.title: Zero Hallucination, by Construction: Hallucination-Aware Layered Oversight for Trustworthy Enterprise AI
2607.17883.paper_summary: Enterprises will not deploy AI agents they cannot trust, and the most-cited reason for distrust is hallucination: confident, fluent output that is simply not true. The common response is to wait for a model that does not hallucinate. We argue that this is the wrong target. Large language models are, by construction, capable of generating unsupported text, and no amount of scale removes the possibility; a faithfulness judge bolted onto a raw model catches some errors but still ships others, and even well-curated retrieval pipelines have been shown to fabricate citations. We reframe the goal: "zero hallucination" is not a property a model possesses but a property a system enforces. We present HALO (Hallucination-Aware Layered Oversight), an assurance architecture which treats hallucination as a containable failure mode rather than an eliminable one. HALO composes six layers of defense: grounded generation over retrieved, approved content; constrained, deterministic execution that bounds where the model can err; multi-signal verification that scores every output for groundedness and hallucination using both an LLM judge and evidence-based checks against the source text; calibrated abstention, so the system declines rather than guesses when grounding is insufficient; total traceability of every retrieval, tool call, and generation; and continuous oversight that detects drift, alerts on threshold breaches, and closes the loop by regenerating and statistically validating improved agents. We detail each layer, give particular attention to evidence-based confidence (which verifies extractions against the source document rather than trusting the model's self-reported certainty), and illustrate the architecture on a regulated claims-extraction workload
2607.17883.paper_summary_zh: 企業不會部署他們無法信任的 AI 代理，而最常被引用的不信任原因是幻覺：自信且流暢的輸出卻根本不真實。常見的回應是等待一個不會產生幻覺的模型。我們認為這是錯誤的目標。大型語言模型在結構上能夠生成不支持的文本，無論規模多大都無法消除這種可能性；一個附加在原始模型上的忠實度評估器能夠捕捉一些錯誤，但仍然會漏掉其他錯誤，甚至即使是精心策劃的檢索管道也已被證明會捏造引用。我們重新定義目標：“零幻覺”不是模型所擁有的特性，而是一個系統所強制執行的特性。我們提出 HALO（幻覺意識分層監管），這是一種保證架構，將幻覺視為可控的失效模式，而不是可消除的模式。HALO 組成了六層防禦：在檢索的、經批准的內容上進行基礎生成；受限的、確定性的執行，界定模型可能出錯的範圍；多信號驗證，對每個輸出進行基礎性和幻覺的評分，使用 LLM 評估器和基於證據的檢查來對照源文本；經過校準的棄權，因此系統在基礎不足時選擇拒絕而不是猜測；每次檢索、工具調用和生成的完全可追溯性；以及持續的監管，檢測漂移，對閾值違規發出警報，並通過重新生成和統計驗證改進的代理來閉合循環。我們詳細介紹每一層，特別關注基於證據的信心（這驗證提取結果是否與源文檔相符，而不是信任模型自我報告的確定性），並在一個受監管的索賠提取工作負載上說明該架構。
